rationale: INCOMING_PY, round 6. The resolution verdict (script/m14/python-endpoint-resolution.ts, per-label decomposition of UNRESOLVED incoming targets) named `references` as one of four labels with an UNEXPLAINED class: 1,454 targets that no reason code, no imported root and no interpreter builtin explains. The largest single shape is `Annotated[T, Field(...)]`, the pydantic/openapi-generator idiom, where the annotation's type expression holds a CALL and the walk that derives `references` recursed into it and published an edge for every identifier it reached — including the keyword-argument NAMES (`min_length`, `strict`, `max_length`, `ge`, `le`). Those are parameter LABELS: they name no type, bind to nothing, and the edge asserts the class references a type called `min_length`, which is a FABRICATED relationship. The independent oracle carried the SAME recursion (oracles/python-truth.ts collectTypeNodes), which is why the differential read green while both sides were wrong — the mirror is the reason the fix had to land in the analyzer AND the oracle in one change. THE RULE: a `keyword_argument` node's NAME child is a label, never a type; its VALUE is still walked, because a real type can live in one (`TypeVar("T", bound=Base)` keeps `Base`), so the fix is a recursion past the name rather than a refusal of the whole call — dropping the call outright would trade a fabrication for a loss. WHAT IS KEPT: the subscript head (`Annotated`) and the called class (`Field`) are names the annotation genuinely mentions, and both stay. The `forbid` rows below are what makes the rule falsifiable in the negative direction: a change that re-widens the walk to keyword names fails here rather than shipping.

expectRelationships.note: the subscript HEAD is a name the annotation mentions; it is imported from typing and stays
the CALLED class inside the validator call is still a name the annotation mentions and is still referenced — the fix drops keyword NAMES, not the callee

forbidRelationships.note: THE HEADLINE FORBID. `min_length` is the name of a keyword argument to `Field`, not a type. Before round 6 this edge existed.
`strict` is a keyword argument NAME; 80+ fabricated edges of this spelling alone were counted in the corpus.
the third keyword NAME on the same line — all three must be gone, not just the first the walk reaches
the second annotated attribute (`Annotated[int, Field(ge=0, le=100)]`) — the rule must hold for every annotation, not for the first one walked
